title: Carbon Fiber BoomBox Material Lab
description: Users operate an interactive material engineering lab where a BoomBox sits on a rotating pedestal. They must apply a carbon fibre texture to specific parts of the BoomBox by selecting mesh regions, adjusting material blend parameters like roughness, metalness, and normal intensity, then validate the final render against target values displayed in a HUD panel.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive material engineering lab. Load BoomBox.glb centered on a circular pedestal at the origin and load CarbonFibre.glb off-screen to extract its texture maps (baseColor, normal, roughness). Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 0.15, 0.4) looking at the origin. Add an HDR-style lighting rig with one DirectionalLight (intensity 2, casting shadows), one HemisphereLight, and one subtle RectAreaLight for reflections. Use OrbitControls with damping enabled, constrained to prevent going below the pedestal. Implement these interaction steps: (1) User clicks a 'Start Lab' button in an HTML overlay panel to begin the session. (2) User clicks on individual mesh children of the BoomBox to select them; highlight selected meshes with an emissive outline effect. (3) A side panel shows sliders for roughness (0.0-1.0), metalness (0.0-1.0), normal map intensity (0.0-2.0), and a carbon fibre blend factor (0.0-1.0). User must adjust each slider and click 'Apply Material' to blend the CarbonFibre textures onto the selected BoomBox meshes using MeshStandardMaterial with mixed maps. (4) User clicks a 'Rotate View' button that animates the camera 360 degrees around the object over 3 seconds using GSAP-style tweening with requestAnimationFrame. (5) User adjusts an environment exposure slider (0.5-3.0) on the renderer's toneMapping exposure. (6) User clicks 'Validate Render' which checks that at least 2 meshes have been modified, roughness is below 0.5, metalness is above 0.6, and blend factor is above 0.3. Display pass/fail results in a styled overlay with green/red indicators for each parameter. Use Raycaster for mesh picking. Render with ACESFilmic tone mapping and sRGB output. Add a subtle animated gradient background using a shader or CSS behind the canvas.
